caption:
Imagine an AI that watches your video like a brain, and tells you it won't hit — before a single stranger sees it.

That's the idea behind Higgsfield AI's newest feature, Virality Predictor, shipped back in May. Higgsfield is already behind a lot of the impossible-camera-move, explosion-transition clips filling your feed — it pulls together 30+ underlying AI video models into one-tap cinematic presets. But this feature does something different. It doesn't generate video. It grades it.

Feed it a clip under 15 seconds and it maps a simulated viewer's attention, memory, and emotional response across the footage, then hands back a virality score, the exact timestamp your hook peaks, a hold rate, and a heatmap of which moments held attention and which lost it. In one tracked test, a 7,000-view video scored higher than a 2.1-million-view one — the tool is reading your specific footage, not just repeating what already went viral.

It replaces the worst part of posting: filming something, publishing blind, then refreshing the view count for two hours wondering if the first three seconds killed it. Now that guessing happens before you hit publish.

There's also a library of Viral Presets ('Red Carpet,' 'Neon City,' high-energy transitions) and Draw-to-Video, which turns a rough sketch into a full animated clip — this isn't only for people chasing ad performance, it's genuinely fun to explore on its own terms.

Worth saying plainly: the 'brain' watching your video is a modeled simulation, not real audience data, so treat the score as a smart signal, not a promise. Higgsfield also built Soul Cast, a compliance tool restricting likeness uploads, after backlash over how reference images were being used — worth knowing going in.

Save this so you don't lose it, and give Virality Predictor a run on your next clip before you post it blind. Full breakdown — link in bio.
